chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me to go to Al-Mufazzal and console him regarding Ismail, and he (peace be upon him) said: Convey greetings to Al-Mufazzal and say to him, We have been bereaved of Ismail, so we were patient; therefore, be patient as we were patient. We intended a matter, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended a matter, so we submitted to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلَ: Ismail, the son of the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of patience in Shia theology regarding the death of the Imams' children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructing Yunus ibn Yakub to convey condolences to al-Mufaddal upon the death of his son, Ismail, highlighting the profound etiquette of bereavement in Shia tradition. The Imam’s phrase 'we were struck by Ismail' (أُصِبْنَا بِإِسْمَاعِيلَ) reflects the specific linguistic and emotional nuance of the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing their personal grief from mere passive endurance. It underscores the theological principle of *taslim* (submission) to divine decree, where the believer aligns their will with Allah’s, a core tenet of Shia spirituality during trials.
